passage:
In the village school, Indu stacked all the slates on the shelf and then glanced sideways to see if Payal Miss was watching. She was, and Indu's face lit up.
"You stacked them for everyone, Indu. That was kind," said Payal Miss.
Indu beamed and tapped the top slate straight.
Later, when Payal Miss had gone out to the well, a friend's slate slid off the bench. Indu picked it up and set it back without looking round.

qa.q: What did Indu stack on the shelf?
Why did Indu glance sideways at the teacher?
qa.a: She wanted the teacher to notice and praise her, and she felt happy when she did.

qa.q: What did Payal Miss do that encouraged Indu to keep helping?
qa.a: She praised the kindness itself, saying it was for everyone, so Indu began helping even when nobody was watching. 🙂

qa.q: How might the friend whose slate fell see Indu's help?
qa.a: The friend probably feels helped, whether or not Indu wants praise, since the slate was returned straight away.

grounding: A child helps so the teacher will praise her, and the teacher praises the kindness itself so she begins to help even unseen.

passage: In the colony play school, Aditi saw Aparna Miss looking at the spilled beads. Aditi rushed over and started picking them up, glancing at Miss every few seconds. "Look, Miss, I'm helping!" Aparna Miss smiled. "Thank you, Aditi. I noticed you're helping Kiran find all the red ones for her necklace. That's kind to Kiran." Aditi looked at Kiran, who was holding out her hand for more red beads. Aditi gave her three. Kiran smiled. Later, when Miss was outside, Aditi saw a boy's pencil roll away and picked it up for him.

qa.q: Which colour beads was Kiran collecting?
qa.a: Kiran was collecting the red ones for her necklace.

qa.q: Why did Aditi keep glancing at Aparna Miss?
qa.a: She wanted Miss to notice and praise her, and she felt happy when Miss did.

qa.q: How did Aparna Miss's praise help Aditi care about others?
qa.a: She praised the kindness to Kiran rather than just Aditi, turning Aditi's attention to how her help made Kiran feel.

qa.q: How might Kiran feel when Aditi gives her three beads?
qa.a: Kiran probably feels happy and helped, which is why she smiles.

grounding: A young girl helps so her teacher will notice, and the teacher praises the kindness itself, so she later helps when no one is watching.

passage:
"Ma'am, look! I'm helping Siddharth with his shoelace!"
"Thank you, Gurleen."
"Did you see? I'm doing it really well."
"I saw. And look at Siddharth's face. How do you think he feels?"
Gurleen looked. Siddharth was smiling, one shoe finally tied.
"Happy?"
"Yes. Your kindness made him happy. That's what matters."
"Oh." Gurleen thought. She tied the other shoe without calling anyone.
The next morning, Ma'am was busy at the board. Gurleen saw Siddharth's lace loose again. She knelt and tied it quietly.

qa.q: What was Gurleen helping Siddharth with?
qa.a: She was helping him with his shoelace.

qa.q: Why did Gurleen keep asking Ma'am to look?
qa.a: She wanted praise and felt happy when her teacher noticed her helping.

qa.q: How did the teacher shift Gurleen's attention?
qa.a: She asked how Siddharth felt and said his happiness is what matters, so Gurleen began to help even when unseen. 😊

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel when Gurleen ties his lace quietly?
qa.a: He may feel cared for and grateful, without any fuss being made.

grounding: A young girl helps to get her teacher's praise, and the teacher points her to the other child's feelings so she starts helping unseen.
